text:
sam: Heads up — I'm proposing a conservative "ingest ceiling" migration for console telemetry next week. Goal: avoid dashboard spikes while we backfill normalized route metrics. Need quick sanity checks on dual-write window and UI fallbacks.

maya: +1 on conservative. can you paste the exact plan? how long is the dual-write? any lockstep UI changes? :thinking_face:

sam: Plan sketch: 1) add route_metrics_v2 table (nullable fields) 2) dual-write from ingest for 48h to allow consumers to opt-in 3) backfill past 7d into v2 with batching/priority 4) after verification flip reads in console for a small subset of orgs 5) ramp reads over 48h. fallback in console via feature flag.

jonathan: Two quick concerns: backfill write throughput (we'll hit the ingest DB CPU) and query plan divergence for dashboards. We should avoid a schema that forces wide row scans.

alex: Can we do an envelope shim instead of a separate table? It'd be cheaper to change the write shape and add an "envelope_version" enum. Backfill becomes lighter. The downside is console ad-hoc SQL might need parsing/env unpacking.

lina: Either approach ok, but dashboard UX needs a stable p99. Whatever we do, the Console should keep showing existing numbers until we've validated parity. Suggest a canary of 5% orgs with feature flag "telemetry.v2_reads" and a dashboard compare panel.

sam: Good notes. Here's the SQL we're planning for the new table (very trimmed):

```sql
CREATE TABLE route_metrics_v2 (
  route_id text PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id text NOT NULL,
  hour_ts timestamptz NOT NULL,
  p50_latency_ms int,
  p95_latency_ms int,
  token_cost numeric,
  attrs jsonb, -- sparse extra fields
  envelope_version int DEFAULT 2
);
```

jonathan: That schema looks fine but we should avoid using jsonb for high-cardinality attrs we index. If we need fast filters, consider a small normalized attrs table keyed by (route_id, attr_key) with aggregated values, or precompute the common filters for the console.

alex: Also: dual-write semantics need idempotency keys. Otherwise backfill + live writes risk duplicates. I'd recommend a write header: `x-ingest-idempotency: ${tenant}:${hour}:${route}` and ingest service dedups on that.

ingest-bot: NOTE: ingest pipeline will throttle backfill jobs if cpu_util > 70% for >10m. Backfill job id: BF-3773.

maya: On the rollout UX: console team wants a toggle per-org and a diff view where we show old vs v2 values for the same time range. That reduces false positives for customers. Can we add that to the plan?

sam: Yes — plan updated: add per-org flag + a dashboard card that shows side-by-side numbers and a delta metric. We'll gate the final cutover when average delta <2% for 24h on the canary orgs.

lina: Who owns the verification queries? We should have a reproducible suite (SQL + threshold checks) that we can run post-backfill. Preferably in an ops repo so we can rerun for postmortems.

jonathan: I'll own the verification suite. Example check: compare sum(token_cost) grouped by hour for a canary org between route_metrics and route_metrics_v2, compute relative error. If > 2% alert and pause rollout.

sam: Good. Also, need to decide on retention: v2 will keep 90 days hot, then compact to weekly aggregates for 1y. Thoughts?

alex: Fine. Make sure the compaction job preserves the same primary keys for the console read layer (i.e., aggregated rows must map cleanly).

maya: Ops question: if we do envelope versioning (alex's suggestion), do we still need a full backfill? maybe only backfill critical aggregates that the console shows. That could cut load by 80%.

sam: That's a great tradeoff. New decision: prefer envelope approach + targeted backfill of console-critical aggregates (p50/p95/token_cost) for last 7 days. Full attr backfill deferred.

lina: Ok — document the deferred work and expected customer-visible gaps. We should also add a migration note for public API consumers (incubation/compatibility).

sam: Will draft the runbook and send for reviews. Thanks everyone. :pray:

ingest-bot: SCHEDULED: Backfill job BF-3773 queued for 2026-04-12T02:00:00Z, window 4h. Monitor: https://internal/ops/jobs/BF-3773

alex: One last implementation nit: add telemetry tags `migration=route_metrics_v2` on all writes so we can filter metrics in Grafana without touching queries. small change, large debuggability win.
